messages.author: af44a577d9ff08de
messages.subject: tooltip with two layers
parts:
Hi all,

Is there a way of restricting a tooltip to a specific layer?

e.g. the code below produces a tooltip when both the line and the points are being hovered over.

In principle, this would be OK, but in this example, when hovering over the line, a constant value of 0.37 is given (the value of y for x = 1).

Ideally, I only want a tooltip when a point is hovered over.

```R
set.seed(101)

df <- data.frame(
  x = 1:10,
  y = round(runif(10), 2)
)

yval <- function(df) sprintf("y value: %s", df$y)

ggvis(df, props(~x, ~y)) +
  layer_point() +
  layer_line() +
  tooltip(yval)
```

Cheers,

Guy

messages.author: 3a42213e2dc51134
messages.subject: Re: tooltip with two layers
parts: I might have a possible workaround. I have a chart with points, a line, and two ribbons. When I put the ribbons later in the code they cover the dots a bit (set to 0.1 opacity). This also has the effect of assigning a "0" tooltip to the entire space covered by the ribbons (incidentally the whole chart). Moving the ribbons to the top of my script moves the dots to the fore (like bring to front in PowerPoint) which then shows only tooltips for my dots and none for the ribbons.
